paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is in charge of every nation, even the ones that think they've got it all figured out. Egypt had its idols, its river and its wise counselors, and Isaiah 19:1 says the idols "will tremble before Him." Verse 12 asks where those wise men are now, and nobody has an answer. Whatever we lean on besides God will wobble, and I've got a few wobbly stamps in my past to prove it.

But watch what the LORD does with the shaking. He strikes Egypt, and then He heals them: "He will strike them but heal them. They will turn to the LORD, and He will hear their prayers and heal them" (Isaiah 19:22). When they cry out because of their oppressors, He sends "a savior and defender to rescue them" (Isaiah 19:20). I think that's the heart of it. God's hand can bring a hard moment, and He is still the One who hears, rescues and heals.

And the ending is the loudest part. Egypt and Assyria, the two nations everybody was afraid of, are called "Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance" (Isaiah 19:25). So none of the people around you are too far gone for the LORD to call His own. When you pray for someone who feels miles away, remember this passage. God's plans are bigger than our guesses, and His welcome is wider than we'd ever dare to hope.
